Let  
\[
L(a,b):=\{x\in V:\{a,b,x\}\in\mathscr H\}
\]
for distinct \(a,b\in V\).

We first recover collinearity from the hypergraph structure.

For distinct \(a,b,c\), translate so that \(a=0\). Write
\[
B(x)=\det(b,x),\qquad C(x)=\det(c,x).
\]

If \(a,b,c\) are noncollinear, then \(B,C\) are independent linear forms, so
\[
x\longmapsto (B(x),C(x))
\]
is a bijection \(V\to\mathbb F_\ell^2\). Hence
\[
|L(a,b)\cap L(a,c)|
=\left(\frac{\ell-1}{2}\right)^2.
\]

If \(a,b,c\) are collinear, write \(c-a=t(b-a)\) with \(t\neq0\). Then
\[
C(x)=tB(x).
\]
Thus
\[
|L(a,b)\cap L(a,c)|
=
\begin{cases}
\ell(\ell-1)/2,&\chi(t)=1,\\
0,&\chi(t)=-1.
\end{cases}
\]

Since \(\ell\ge5\), the three possible values
\[
0,\qquad \frac{(\ell-1)^2}{4},\qquad \frac{\ell(\ell-1)}2
\]
are distinct. Therefore the relation \(\mathscr H\) determines which triples are collinear. Every \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathscr H)\) is consequently a collineation of the affine plane \(V\).

By the fundamental theorem of affine geometry, every bijective collineation of \(\mathbb F_\ell^2\) is affine semilinear. Since \(\mathbb F_\ell\) is prime, it has no nontrivial field automorphisms, so
\[
\sigma(x)=Ax+b
\]
with \(A\in\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)\), \(b\in V\).

For such a map,
\[
\det\bigl(A(v-u),A(w-u)\bigr)
=\det(A)\det(v-u,w-u).
\]
Thus \(\sigma\) preserves \(\mathscr H\) exactly when \(\det(A)\) is a nonzero square. Hence
\[
\operatorname{Aut}(\mathscr H)
=
V\rtimes \{A\in\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell):\chi(\det A)=1\}.
\]

Now consider \(f(x)=Ax+b\). A fixed point satisfies
\[
(I-A)x=b.
\]

If \(1\) is not an eigenvalue of \(A\), then \(I-A\) is invertible and \(f\) has exactly one fixed point.

If \(A=I\), then \(f\) is fixed-point-free precisely when \(b\neq0\), giving
\[
\ell^2-1
\]
maps.

If \(A\neq I\) has eigenvalue \(1\), then \(\operatorname{rank}(I-A)=1\). Therefore \(f\) is fixed-point-free precisely when \(b\notin\operatorname{im}(I-A)\), giving
\[
\ell^2-\ell=\ell(\ell-1)
\]
choices of \(b\).

It remains to count such matrices \(A\) with square determinant.

For each square \(d\neq1\), matrices with eigenvalues \(1,d\) form one conjugacy class of size
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)|}{(\ell-1)^2}
=\ell(\ell+1).
\]
There are
\[
\frac{\ell-3}{2}
\]
such values \(d\).

For \(d=1\), the nonidentity matrices with eigenvalue \(1\) are the nontrivial unipotent matrices, forming one conjugacy class of size
\[
\frac{|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)|}{\ell(\ell-1)}
=\ell^2-1.
\]

Thus the number \(N\) of relevant nonidentity matrices is
\[
N=\ell(\ell+1)\frac{\ell-3}{2}+(\ell^2-1)
=\frac{(\ell+1)^2(\ell-2)}2.
\]

Therefore the number of fixed-point-free automorphisms is
\[
(\ell^2-1)+\ell(\ell-1)N.
\]
Substituting \(N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\ell^2-1)+\ell(\ell-1)\frac{(\ell+1)^2(\ell-2)}2
&=\frac{(\ell-1)^2(\ell+1)(\ell^2-2)}2.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{(\ell-1)^2(\ell+1)(\ell^2-2)}{2}}
\]
